title: config:write:set passes readCascade to validators
detail: The set handler binds readCascade to the config resolver, the tenant-scoped db and the secrets reader, so validators see the same cascade as the value queries.

title: config:query:values and config:query:cascade accept a read scope
detail: Both queries take an optional scope (system, tenant, user). With scope system the cascade of a tenant or user key is evaluated at system level, so the system row is returned even when the caller's own tenant has a row for the key. Only a SystemAdmin gets the narrowed read; other callers keep the normal cascade. Inherited-value redaction still applies. Without scope the behavior is unchanged.

title: Remove unreachable branch in configRowHoldsValue
detail: The undefined key definition is now handled together with the plaintext comparison, dropping a dead return without changing behavior.

title: Config key validate() receives a db scoped to the written tenant
detail: A SystemAdmin writing a config value for another tenant previously handed the validator a system-mode db that could read every tenant. `ConfigValidateContext.db` is now a `TenantDb` locked to the tenant the value is written for. The validator runs inside the write transaction, so a slow query there should set its own timeout.

title: config keys can declare an async write validator that rejects with a KumikoError
detail: Config key definitions accept a new async `validate(value, ctx)` function. `config:write:set` runs it after the type, bounds and pattern checks and before the value is stored, for every scope and backing. A validator rejects the write by throwing a `KumikoError`, for example an `UnprocessableError`. The feature manifest reports `validated` per key.
migration: No action needed: keys without `validate` behave as before.

title: config:write:set masks the echoed value for encrypted-at-rest keys; validation errors no longer include the value
migration: A caller that reads `data.value` from a `config:write:set` result for a key with `encrypted: true` or `backing: "secrets"` now gets the mask. Use the value it sent instead. Tests that match the `value` param of a validation error on such a key need to drop that expectation.

title: Extension-selector settings render as one tenant screen
detail:
BREAKING: an extension-selector key now renders as a select of the mounted plugin ids, and
`config:write:set` rejects every value except a mounted plugin id or "" with 422
`config.errors.unknownExtensionPlugin`.

The owner's tenant screen `<owner>-tenant` is now a dashboard; its former configEdit moved
to `<owner>-tenant-selection`. Plugin features under a masked selector lose their tenant nav
entry: their `<plugin>-tenant` screen stays as a nav-less embedded panel (a direct deep link
still resolves), and their secrets move from the global `secrets` screen into
`<plugin>-tenant-secrets` panels. A plugin feature registered under more than one selector
registration keeps the previous behaviour.

Generated hub screens need the new key `config.settings.extensionSelectorHint` (shipped in
the config and secrets bundles, en/de/es).
migration:
Links, tests or screenshots that open `<plugin>-tenant` through the nav or expect a configEdit
at `<owner>-tenant` should open `<owner>-tenant` (now the dashboard) and look for the plugin
panels there. Tenant rows or scripts that write a selector value naming no mounted plugin must
write a mounted plugin id or "" instead. No new translation keys are required from apps.

title: systemScope handlers get a default per-tenant+handler rate limit; the four read queries opt out (fw#2861).
detail: `config` mounts under `r.systemScope()`, so `config:write:set`/`config:write:reset` without their own `rateLimit` now default to `{ per: "tenant+handler", limit: 600, windowSeconds: 60 }` once an app has a `RateLimitResolver` configured (framework change, see kumiko-framework changes.json 0.271.0). `config:query:cascade`, `config:query:values`, `config:query:schema` and `config:query:readiness` declare `rateLimit: { disabled: true, reason: "..." }` — each is a self-scoped read of the caller's own readable config, hit on every page load, and a per-tenant bucket would throttle the whole tenant's page loads instead of just that one handler's traffic.

title: Reencrypt job: removed legacy-decrypt path
detail: The old single-key format (CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY) is no longer supported. The reencrypt job now classifies rows as rotate/current/unrecognized — unreadable rows are counted as failed instead of silently attempted.
migration: If any config values still exist in the old single-key format, re-encrypt them with the current envelope format before upgrading. The job will now throw an error instead of attempting migration.
